**W37**: "What's up?" / "Look there. If that doesn't beat the band!" — The opening "What's up?" is a response to something (Julius halting) not in this window. This is a connective/definite dangle, but per instructions short dialogue responses are a known limitation. However, "What's up?" as an opener with no prior action in the window is a connective dangle — the exclamation "If that doesn't beat the band!" references something being seen, but "there" has no referent inside the window.

**W31**: "Can't be. We'd see him." / "Nevertheless Tommy's sense of the enemy's omniscience deepened." — "Nevertheless" opens the second paragraph contrasting with something not in the window (the reassurance). But both sentences are in the window — the nevertheless connects to "Can't be" which IS in the window. Fine.

**W11**: "The gravity of his tone impressed Tommy" — "his tone" refers to someone speaking before this window opens. This is a pronoun/definite dangle on "his tone" with no antecedent inside the window.

**W10**: "You are still young, Mr. Hersheimmer..." — Sir James is quoted but not introduced in this window; per instructions named characters are tracked. Fine.

**W32**: "Nevertheless Tommy's sense of the enemy's omniscience deepened." — "Nevertheless" contrasts with prior material not in this window (the reassurance "Can't be"). Connective dangle.

**W46**: "'That's it—for sure,' breathed Julius." — This is a response to something pointed at/said before this window. "When I was in France..." then Tommy glares at "the rock" — "the rock" has no antecedent in this window. Definite article dangle.

**W57**: "Tommy held steady until the heat had done its work, then withdrew it—only to utter a cry." — "it" refers to the paper being held near heat, not established in this window. Pronoun dangle.
